title: Chest Pain
hpi_narrative: {{patient_name}} presents with acute onset chest pain, palpitations, shortness of breath, diaphoresis, nausea, and sense of impending doom. Symptoms peak within minutes and occur in discrete episodes. The patient has a history of similar episodes and significant anxiety about future attacks (anticipatory anxiety). This is a panic attack — a psychiatric diagnosis but one that requires thorough medical evaluation because patients often present to the ED with cardiac concerns. Key: rule out MI, PE, arrhythmia, hyperthyroidism, pheochromocytoma, and substance-induced anxiety. ECG, troponin, CXR, TSH, and toxicology screen are appropriate. If negative and history consistent, panic disorder is the diagnosis. Treatment: SSRIs (first-line: sertraline, paroxetine, escitalopram) + CBT. Benzodiazepines for short-term acute management only (risk of dependence). Reassurance and psychoeducation are therapeutic.
chief_complaint: Acute chest pain, palpitations, SOB, sense of impending doom

stacks.label: Physical Exam: Heart / Cardiovascular
stacks.finding: Chest pain — assess cardiac. Tachycardia common in panic.

stacks.label: ECG, 12 lead
stacks.finding: Rule out MI/arrhythmia — may show sinus tachycardia only.

stacks.label: Cardiac troponin
stacks.finding: Rule out MI — must be negative to differentiate from ACS.

stacks.label: Toxicology screen, urine
stacks.finding: Rule out substance-induced anxiety (cocaine, amphetamines, PCP).

stacks.label: Reassure patient / Psychoeducation
stacks.finding: Explain diagnosis — panic attacks are real physiological events but not dangerous. Education is therapeutic.

stacks.label: SSRI (Sertraline / Paroxetine / Escitalopram)
stacks.finding: First-line for panic disorder. Start low, titrate slow.

stacks.label: Refer to psychiatry / CBT
stacks.finding: CBT is gold standard psychotherapy for panic disorder. Psychiatry follow-up for medication management.

physical_exam.psychiatric: Sense of impending doom. Fear of dying, losing control. Anticipatory anxiety about future attacks.

decoys.label: Benzodiazepines as sole long-term treatment
decoys.reason_wrong: Benzos are for short-term acute management only (risk of dependence, tolerance, withdrawal). SSRIs are first-line for long-term panic disorder. CBT is essential.

decoys.label: Discharge without cardiac workup
decoys.reason_wrong: Must rule out MI, PE, arrhythmia, hyperthyroidism, and substance-induced anxiety. Panic attack is a diagnosis of exclusion in the ED.

teach_me_steps.reasoning: Must rule out MI (ECG, troponin), PE, hyperthyroidism (TSH), substance-induced (tox screen). Panic: discrete episodes peaking in minutes, fear of dying/losing control, anticipatory anxiety.
SSRI first-line (sertraline, paroxetine). CBT is gold standard psychotherapy. Benzos only short-term/acute. Psychoeducation reduces fear.

case_summary: Panic attack. Chest pain + palpitations + SOB + impending doom. ECG/troponin/CXR/TSH all normal. Reassurance + SSRIs + CBT referral. Rule out cardiac before diagnosing panic.
